rationale: Natural handoff after two completed obligations on the commit context of a node that adopts snapshot state. The map still recorded the follower commit context of the install path as a deferred surface and carried no entry at all for the construction-time restore path, although both have now been selected, executed and confirmed: obligation c-snapshot-install-commit-context was served by check d3999c33daf64a04949efbadb3e6f5e2 (a node that installed a source-produced snapshot at index 43 published commit_index 0 while applied_index and last_index were 43) and obligation c-snapshot-restore-commit-context by check 6c982b1fcb114ff7b3e4b22ace5a238b (the same node, reconstructed over its own stores, reported last_snapshot_index 43 and published commit_index 0 while applied_index and last_index were 43). This product replaces the answered deferred surface with its sourced disposition and adds the recovery entry point beside it, so the overview no longer lists as unread a path that has been checked. No fact, behaviour, activity or core-path object changes, and no repaired result is claimed.

surface:Raft.installSnapshot on the foll.rationale: The surface moves from deferred to mapped because the question it recorded has been selected and answered: the obligation fixes that a node installing a snapshot carrying committed state through J must publish a commit context at least J, and the served check observed the contrary for a snapshot at index 43, with the node publishing commit_index 0 while reporting applied and last as 43. The entry keeps pointing at the installing behaviour and at the client contract that reports the value.
surface:Raft.installSnapshot on the foll.preserves: The entry point, its high-consequence flag and its association with the instalment path are unchanged; only the disposition, the behaviour association and the reason are refreshed to record the answered question.

surface:NewRaft startup restoreSnapshot.rationale: Additive entry recording the second entry point of the same publication duty, which the previous Candidate had already named as support but the map did not carry as a surface: construction-time recovery publishes lastApplied and lastSnapshot from the stored snapshot and never writes the commit index, and the served check observed a node that had reported index 43 as committed, applied and last before the restart publishing commit_index 0 afterwards while reporting last_snapshot_index 43.

feedback.answered: A node that adopts committed snapshot state publishes a commit context below the state it has taken as applied, on both entry points that were investigated. On the runtime path, an InstallSnapshot delivered through the module's own transport at index 43 left the receiver publishing commit_index 0 with applied_index and last_index 43 (check d3999c33daf64a04949efbadb3e6f5e2, artifact 5448e685a3844063a9d626fe7045b729). On the recovery path, the same node reconstructed over its own stores reported restored true and last_snapshot_index 43 yet published commit_index 0 with applied_index and last_index 43 and the identical Stats pair (check 6c982b1fcb114ff7b3e4b22ace5a238b, artifact 32d511373b4a46d9a7d55597b3e632f0). Both were confirmed after review with no open issue, and in both the published value is the one Raft.CommitIndex() and Stats report, so the under-report is in the library's own export path and not in the observation.
remaining: The repair location for both entry points stays open: advancing the commit index when the snapshot state is adopted, or deriving the published value from the last snapshot index, are both consistent with the two obligations and neither is sourced.
Which consumer outside the module relies on the published commit index of a follower or a restarted node, which would raise the consequence beyond the client-contract reading, was not established.

The deferred surface 'Transport.SetHeartbeatHandler (any caller or third-party transport)' still records that the concurrency contract of transports other than the two shipped ones is unread; the confirmed term-regression finding covers the shipped NetworkTransport and InmemTransport paths only.

The deferred surface 'LogStore.MonotonicLogStore and snapshot compaction interplay' still records that removeOldLogs and compactLogsWithTrailing were read only at the call sites used by the snapshot behaviours, so the effect of a non-monotonic store on history reconstruction remains unmapped.
The nested modules fuzzy/ and raft-compat/ remain outside the single module selected for execution and were never read.
feedback.rationale: The two obligations answered the commit-context question for the entry points the earlier Candidate recorded, so the map's install surface is no longer deferred and the recovery entry point is now recorded beside it. Everything else in the overview - the two core relationships, the fact and behaviour relations, and the remaining deferred surfaces - is retained unchanged, and the remaining list keeps the open repair choices and the unread surfaces visible rather than presenting the answered paths as resolved designs.
